Main feature for them is pane splitting, set up to work like Tilix; the Lua config is very intuitive. Downsides: occasional indirect crashes when Xwayland crashes, and they had to disable Wayland support because the window decorations aren't great yet.
Complaint: iTerm2 has a hotkey quake-style visor mode, WezTerm doesn't. Replies point to a workaround in GitHub issue #1751 and to using Hammerspoon on macOS to toggle the app.
Moved to WezTerm from kitty and is very happy. WezTerm is 'leaps and bounds better' out of the box; their config fits on one screen, and then the terminal 'just gets out of the way'.

Long-time tmux user with persistent mouse issues switched to WezTerm and the problems went away. Pane splitting and resizing are fast, and copying from a vertical split doesn't grab the other pane. Downside: mouse themes apply inconsistently on GNOME/Wayland.
Favorite, often-overlooked feature: WezTerm is fully cross-OS. They work across Linux, macOS and Windows, learn one terminal, and share large parts of the config between OSes.

Long-time iTerm2 user saw it slow to over a second to appear on cmd-tab. Finds WezTerm fast and very configurable. Only trouble: cmd-left/cmd-right had to be added manually in the Lua config instead of being defaults.

Wez has been 'shockingly responsive' to GitHub issues, usually fixing real problems within a day or two. Only minor quibbles with modifier keys over SSH. Switched from Alacritty for better modifier support with remote emacs.
Main complaint is discoverability: they looked up keyboard copy mode once, forgot it, and went back to mouse selection, even though the docs are good and the author is helpful.
Tried WezTerm on Windows for ligatures and lower latency than Windows Terminal, but its input latency was still higher than cmd.exe.

Loves the quick select/copy modes (C-S-Space, then type the letters shown). Uses it as mosh+tmux-like reconnectable sessions with panes and tabs from a Mac laptop to a Linux work machine: 'top notch'.
Used WezTerm for its cross-platform support and Lua config, but switched to Ghostty because WezTerm's image support didn't play well with tmux.
Keeps a single WezTerm config, wraps it in a nix expression for home-manager/NixOS, and symlinks it on Windows as a portal to WSL. Tooling stays consistent across all machines.
On macOS iTerm2 is unmatched for this user; the closest they found was WezTerm, 'and even that is a pale shadow of iTerm2'.
Uses 2-5 Macs. Syncing iTerm2 settings with chezmoi was next to impossible; with WezTerm the config is just Lua code, easy to diff and apply.

On macOS, WezTerm's latency was noticeably higher than Kitty's and it often painted lines as blank in vim, forcing a return to Kitty. On Linux, though, they love WezTerm over Kitty and had none of these issues.
Reasons given over Alacritty: ligatures, copy mode, hyperlinks, native scrollback with a scrollbar, native tabs, and lower OpenGL/GLES requirements so it runs on Arm64 hardware without hassle.
Complaint about size: WezTerm is 224 MB on their Mac vs 74 MB for iTerm2 and 10 MB for Terminal, though they've used and loved WezTerm for over a year.
Tried WezTerm after positive HN reviews and found it 'severely lacking in font configuration department'.
Odd quirks: no menus on macOS, and on Linux a hyperminimal tiling-WM-style titlebar instead of the WM's. Feels targeted at i3/Sway/vim users rather than general users.
Completely replaced tmux with WezTerm on Linux and Mac, and it also works on Windows with ported tmux keybindings.
